script: Britain built a real plan to kill Hitler with a single sniper shot, then buried it for fifty years. In 1944, intelligence learned Hitler took the same solitary walk near his mountain retreat almost every morning. Officers proposed dropping a trained sniper by parachute to end the war with one bullet. The plan, Operation Foxley, was fully approved, weapon tested, route mapped. Then British command quietly killed it, afraid a dead Hitler would be replaced by a general who ran the war better. The file stayed sealed for decades. When it finally opened in 1998, historians realized Britain had a clean shot years early, and chose not to take it.

description:
Operation Foxley was Britain's real, fully-approved 1944 plan to assassinate Hitler with a single sniper during his daily mountain walk. It was scrapped -- and hidden until 1998.
